pairs.difference: Both silhouettes are plain circles with the same straight_share, corner_rate and solidity. The only form difference is the valve cap: small and flat on A, wide on B. That is too little to choose on.

A's target is a fat disc with a thick, swollen blue edge, sitting on a chunky easel with stubby legs. B's target has a thinner rim and a plainer stand. The bears are about equal. The call rests only on the plumper disc.
pairs.fix: Draw the target as a thin flat board with a narrow straight edge, on a slim wooden easel with thin legs.

pairs.difference: B's unit is deeper and heavier, with a bulging left end, and the silhouette shows a louvre tab hanging off the underside. It also adds side vent slots, the extra detail seen on the generated computers in the lessons. A is slimmer and longer with a plain end cap, though its corners are soft too.
pairs.fix: Draw a long, slim wall unit with a shallow body, flat front and tight corners. Keep the end panel plain and tuck the louvre into the body.

pairs.difference: B is a tidy, compact block (solidity 0.944) with extra rivets and corner plates, and the coin pile and lid close the outline into one mass. A is simpler and has a more broken outline, with a separate lid and a visible gap, though its gold bands are soft. The lean is weak.
pairs.fix: Keep the chest simple with fewer rivets. Open the lid well clear of the box so a clear gap shows, with flat plank faces and narrow straight metal bands.

pairs.difference: A's white crown is a fat pillow and its visor is a thick, heavy slab, so the cap reads as a toy. B's crown is leaner and its visor thins to a fine curved edge at the left tip.
pairs.fix: Slim the crown so it slopes evenly, and draw the visor as a thin curved plate with a fine edge.

pairs.difference: A's roof is a tall, swollen dome over a booth with rounded lower corners and bulging feet on the base. B has a shallow roof, straight vertical sides and a crisp flat base with tight corners.
pairs.fix: Lower the roof to a shallow curve, and keep the booth sides straight with a flat, square-cornered plinth and no bulging feet.

pairs.difference: B's gloves are ballooned: the left one is a huge bean with a separate ball-like thumb, the wrist cuffs are shrunken, and the two gloves merge into one mass. A's gloves have clear thumbs, proper cuff bands and a notch separating the pair.
pairs.fix: Draw two separate boxing gloves with a modest padded fist, a thumb that lies against the fist, and a clear wide wrist cuff with a strap.

pairs.difference: B's blades are fat paddles with rounded blob ends and a swollen orange rim, and the two fins touch. A's blades are slim and taper to a split tip with a notch and thin side rails, with a clear gap between the fins.
pairs.fix: Draw narrow tapered fin blades with thin side rails, a flat tip and a clear gap between the two fins.

pairs.difference: B enlarges the props like toys: a huge ring buoy that is wider than the deck and wrapped around a post, a thick rope coil, and massive square posts. A keeps a small buoy hanging from a post, with a visible deck and thin railings, though its posts are stubby.
pairs.fix: Make the ring buoy small, hanging from a post. Show a long plank deck with thin rails and slimmer posts.

pairs.difference: A's fronds are fat rounded mitts on a thick trunk, which is an inflated toy look. B's fronds are narrow and pointed on a slimmer trunk, though they are over-numerous and radiate stiffly. Solidity is close on both, so this is a lean only.
pairs.fix: Slim the fronds into long, narrow tapering leaves with sharp cuts, on a thinner curved trunk.

pairs.difference: A's locker has soft, blobby corners at the top and on the door, a thick swollen door, sausage-like vent bars and stub feet. Its solidity of 0.961 is at the top of the real range. B has a flat top lid with a crisp edge, planar sides, thin slot vents, hinges and a slimmer door.
pairs.fix: Draw flat sheet-metal panels with tight corner bevels, a thin door, narrow slot vents and small hinges.

pairs.difference: B's slide is a fat tube with thick column supports, and the platform is reduced to a slab under a lump at the top. Its outline is one heavy mass. A has a narrower chute, thin braces, a railed platform and an open ladder, though its thin_share of 0.045 is above the real range.
pairs.fix: Narrow the chute and use thin support posts with braces, plus a small platform with thin railings.

pairs.difference: B's body is a swollen cushion with a bulged outline and very soft corners, topped by a big disc button, and its wires bunch together. A's body is a smaller rounded box with straighter sides, a stepped inset panel and a single clear plug, with the wires separated and earbuds on slim stems.
pairs.fix: Make the player a thinner box with straighter sides and tight corners. Run two separate thin wires to earbuds on slim stems.

pairs.difference: B's envelope is a puffed pillow with bulging sides and large soft corners, and its bottom-left and right corners are blobs. A's envelope is a flat sheet with straight edges, tight corners and crisp fold lines (corner_rate 4.31 vs 2.56).
pairs.fix: Draw a flat paper envelope with straight edges, sharp small corners and thin crease lines, with no puffing.

pairs.difference: B's glass plate has a thick slab rim and the fruit sits in a dense heap. A's plate is a thin shallow dish with a fine rim, and the fruit parts stay distinct. The lens lost B's plate, so this rests on the colour image only.
pairs.fix: Draw a thin shallow glass plate with a fine rim.

pairs.difference: B's wreath is thick with a small hole and carries an oversized bow, and the door adds an arch and blocky plinths. A has a slim wreath ring with a wide opening, and a flat rectangular door with straight panels and sharp rails. B's mask is smeared and A's shows only the wreath, so the silhouette is weak evidence.
pairs.fix: Make the wreath a slim ring with a wide opening and a small bow, on a flat rectangular panelled door.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away through inflation. Forms are fatter and more compact than the real ones: envelopes and player bodies swell into pillows, fin blades into paddles, slides into thick tubes, gloves into balloons. Corners go soft and blobby where real cards keep tight bevels. Thin parts such as rims, visors, braces and rails thicken or close up, so the outline merges into one heavy mass with few gaps. They also add props and detail, such as side vents, rivets and hinged extras, and enlarge them. Real cards stay simpler, keep planar faces, and leave clear openings between parts.
